original.target_description: Target analytic sample unresolved: task-phase or pooled theta rhythmicity test versus experiment-specific studies 1 and 5.

n.sample_role: Participants for second-level O-score analyses; repeated participant-by-task-phase observations in the pooled mixed model; target unit not uniquely selected.
n.exclusions: Chance-level catch accuracy and fewer than 10 correct button presses exclude participants by task phase. Final target-specific counts unavailable in supplied text.
n.location: Methods: Task versions; Assessment of performance and exclusion of participants; Results: Behavioral responses oscillate at theta frequencies for memory-dependent task phases (Fig. 3A); Fig. 1C caption. Cached HTML has no printed page markers.
n.quote: The numbers of participants per task version and their demographic information is given in Fig. 1 and Supplementary Table 1 . ... The data of a participant were only included in the analysis of a task phase if the following two requirements were met: (1) catch question accuracy across trials exceeding chance level and (2) a minimum of 10 correct button presses per participant in the task phase of interest. ... The number of participants included in each of the task phases is shown in Fig. 1 and the number of excluded participants can be found in Supplementary Fig. 1A .

notes: Identity verified independently in supplied canonical text: full primary Nature Communications HTML article, title Theta rhythmicity governs human behavior and hippocampal signals during memory-dependent tasks; Marije ter Wal and the listed coauthors; volume 12, article 7048 (2021); DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-27323-3. Results, Methods, references and data-availability sections are present. This is not an abstract or secondary report. Figure captions are present but graphical Fig. 1C counts and Supplementary Table 1 are not supplied; no PDF was named. Only n_o is assigned; all other fields/sides are unassigned placeholders. The neutral description and p. 4 locator do not uniquely identify one critical test: the source reports five task-phase O-score tests, a pooled mixed model of O-score strength, and another mixed model of peak frequency. The supplied study identifier 1,5 may instead refer to constituent experiments; the source identifies experiment 1 as visual and experiment 5 as memory, but directs experiment-specific participant counts to Supplementary Table 1. This table and the numeric Fig. 1C image are not present in the supplied text. Reported group counts precede phase-specific exclusions and are not explicit final groups for an identified critical test. Therefore no analytic N is assigned. Participant counts and repeated participant-by-phase observations must be distinguished; no N is derived from df, recruitment totals, percentages, or subtraction of exclusions. Candidate context only: memory groups 1 and 2 have reported n=71 and n=155 before exclusions; separate visual group 3 n=95. Twelve memory-task participants were excluded for chance-level performance; another 32 encoding and 1 retrieval participants with sufficient performance were excluded for low trial counts. These are not a permitted sum of mutually exclusive final groups. Candidate tests (not selected): Encoding t(181)=6.20, Retrieval t(68)=4.58, Catch-with-retrieval t(143)=5.08, all p<0.001; Catch-after-retrieval t(69)=1.69, p=0.240; Visual t(94)=-4.10, p=1.00 (Bonferroni-corrected for five comparisons). Pooled O-score model: coefficient=0.28, 95% CI 0.19–0.36, t(556)=6.55, p<0.001. Peak-frequency model: coefficient=-5.09, 95% CI -7.52 to 2.67, t(371)=6.55, p<0.001, as printed. None establishes experiment-1/5 analytic N. No arithmetic performed.
